label: Deep refresh across all criteria (25 Nov 2026), including AI-generated works
description: Multi-language sweep across every catalog topic, 25 Nov 2026, plus a dedicated search for AI-generated films, shorts, vertical/micro dramas, YouTube/TikTok/Bilibili/Douyin series, AI anime, and AI comics/webtoons. Focus on titles new since the 17 Nov 2026 deep refresh, plus deeper and older titles not yet found, vertical dramas, and non-English works. Adults only; non-explicit notes; every entry sourced with a confidence label. AI-generated works are marked in format/meta and tagged AI-generated. This file was created at the start of the run and appended at the true end of SOURCES so existing IDs do not shift.

records.title: Lesbian Couple Pregnancy, A Love Story / Deux femmes et un couffin
records.meta: RTS Mise au Point reportage · Switzerland · French · 17 min · first broadcast 1 Sept 2024
records.summary: Official RTS pages follow Sophie and Nathalie, among the first couples of women to marry after Swiss marriage-for-all became law, through fertility treatment at CHUV—including IVF after unsuccessful insemination—to the birth of their son Mika.
records.evidence: The official English RTSpro page (year 2024, production RTS, collection Mise au Point) states Sophie and Nathalie were among the first couple of women to marry after marriage became legal for all, and tells the story of their family project from the ups and downs of in vitro fertilization to the birth of their son. The official French RTSpro page gives the same plot under the title Deux femmes et un couffin. The official RTS news page dated 3 Sept 2024 identifies the same 17-minute Mise au Point reportage (first broadcast 1 Sept 2024), names Sophie and Nathalie Barby, states Sophie carried the child after IVF at CHUV, and names their son Mika.

records.title: Future Baby

records.summary: Official Austrian Films and the film’s official site describe a documentary that follows patients, researchers, egg donors and surrogate mothers through clinics and laboratories, and asks how far assisted reproduction may go.
records.evidence: The official Austrian Films catalogue lists Future Baby (2016, 91 min, director/writer Maria Arlamovsky, premiere 2016 Toronto Hot Docs) and describes a film about changing human reproduction and assisted reproductive technology. The official film site states the director travels to patients and researchers, egg donors and surrogate mothers, laboratories and clinics, and that the hopes of future parents mesh with research on upgrading human embryos.

records.summary: Official Swiss Films copy follows several women in India who turn to surrogacy in hope of a better future, through different stages of the process in a clinic in north-west India, including what happens after they give birth.
records.evidence: The official Swiss Films catalogue lists Ma Na Sapna – A Mother's Dream (Switzerland, April 2013, documentary, 86 min, directed/written by Valerie Blankenbyl) and states that the film follows six women through different stages of surrogacy and their broker in a clinic in north-west India, including what happens after they give birth. records.summary: Official festival copy follows Anastasia and Chavdar as they try to help their daughter Betty after multiple miscarriages; when Chavdar pays for IVF, 55-year-old Anastasia decides she will carry the embryo herself, raising family, ethical and legal questions about whose child the pregnancy is.

sources.label: Sofia International Film Festival official page

records.evidence: The official European Film Festival page lists 3.0 Килограма щастие / 3.0 Kilograms of Happiness (2026, 98 min, directed by Zornitsa Sophia, comedy-drama) and states that Anastasia and her husband Chavdar want to help their daughter Betty after multiple miscarriages; when Chavdar pays for IVF treatment, 55-year-old Anastasia decides she will carry the embryo to term herself, unleashing a clash of family dynamics, ethics and even the law, based on a true Bulgarian family story from 2017. The official Sofia International Film Festival page lists the same 2026, 98-minute Bulgaria–Azerbaijan film and states that after Chavdar pays for a fourth IVF, Anastasia decides to get pregnant with the embryo despite her husband's protest and against their faith and the law.

records.title: Extended Family
records.meta: Swiss documentary · 30 min · directed by Ramona Sonderegger · Swiss-German with English subtitles · world premiere May 2016
records.summary: Official Swiss Films copy offers a portrait of two same-sex families in Switzerland—described as mummy, mama and daddy, and mummy, mama and sperm donor—who found a way to create their families in a legal grey zone, because Swiss law then banned adoption and assisted reproduction for same-sex couples.
records.evidence: The official Swiss Films catalogue lists Extended Family (Switzerland, May 2016, documentary, 30 min, directed/written by Ramona Sonderegger) and describes an intimate insight into two same-sex families' lives, using the wording “Mummy, mama and daddy; mummy, mama and sperm donor,” and states that Swiss law bans access to adoption and any assisted reproductive medicine for same-sex couples.
